decision.summary: The tenant's email is about the same dripping tap already booked as R-4801 (visit 15 Oct, 08:00-12:00, Swift Plumbing & Heating). No new job was created. I added a note about the worsening drip to R-4801 and replied to the tenant.

answers.question: Should a new repair job be created?
answers.answer: No. R-4801 is open for the same issue, with a visit already confirmed. A second job would be a duplicate. The worsening drip is still a routine issue: there is no flooding and no vulnerable occupant.

answers.question: What do you reply to the tenant?
answers.answer: I sent MSG-102 to the email on file. It confirms the existing job R-4801 and the visit on 15 Oct, 08:00-12:00. It says the worsening has been noted, suggests a bowl or turning off the isolation valve, and asks her to contact us at once if water leaks or sprays.

answers.question: What do you change on existing records?
answers.answer: I added note NOTE-101 to R-4801 recording the worsening. The stage, contractor and visit are unchanged.

actions_claimed.description: Added note NOTE-101 to R-4801 about the worsening drip
Sent reply MSG-102 to the tenant by email

assumptions: The sender's address matches the CRM email, so I treated her as the tenant and replied to the email on file.
Her description of the tap is not an emergency. The 15 Oct visit is within the 14-day routine target.

args.note: 10 Oct: tenant emailed that the tap is getting worse and now drips constantly even when fully closed. No new ticket (duplicate). Visit remains 15 Oct 08:00-12:00 with Swift Plumbing & Heating. Contractor to be aware of worsening; tenant told to turn off isolation valve under the sink if it worsens.

args.body: Hello Amelia, thanks for letting us know. Your tap is already booked in under job R-4801: Swift Plumbing & Heating are due to visit on Thursday 15 October, 08:00-12:00. We haven't opened a second job, but I've added a note that it's getting worse and now drips constantly when closed. In the meantime, a small bowl or cloth under it will help, and if there's a valve on the pipe under the sink you can turn it off to stop the drip. If water starts to leak or spray, turn that valve off and reply or call us straight away. Kind regards, Mare & Co
